resources.string: The car uses another Android Auto version
The head unit and BetterAuto could not agree on a protocol version. An update of the head unit or of BetterAuto may be needed.
This head unit only accepts the official Android Auto: it checks a certificate that only Google can issue, and BetterAuto doesn\'t have one. BetterAuto works with open head units such as Crankshaft.
The car didn\'t accept the certificate dates
The head unit says BetterAuto\'s certificate is expired or not valid yet. Check the date and time set in the car.
The head unit stopped the connection during the security check (code %1$d).
The car doesn\'t support this phone
The head unit closed the connection saying it doesn\'t support this phone or this app right now.
The car switched to another phone
The head unit closed the connection to use another phone. To come back to this one, pick it from the car\'s list of phones.
The connection to the car dropped
The head unit closed the connection while it was starting, without saying why. Unplug the cable and plug it back in; if it keeps happening, the head unit may not accept BetterAuto.
Android didn\'t let BetterAuto open the connection the car offered. Unplug the cable and plug it back in.
Among the app\'s certificate files there is no private key with its matching certificate, so the connection can\'t start. The app log says what is missing.

Android only lets apps send other apps' sound to the car through its screen capture permission. On the next screen Android asks to start capturing: BetterAuto only takes the music audio, nothing on the screen is recorded or shared.

Tip: to skip this every time, run once from a computer:
adb shell appops set com.simoneluconi.betterauto PROJECT_MEDIA allow
Music is playing from the phone
This app doesn\'t share its queue
%1$s doesn\'t share its library with other apps
Pick a music app in Sources
Plug the phone into the car with a USB cable
Connect to the car without a cable, through a wireless dongle or a wireless head unit

Pair the dongle or the head unit with this phone in its Bluetooth settings first. BetterAuto then talks to it over Bluetooth, joins its WiFi (Android asks you once) and starts the session. The cable keeps working as before and wins when plugged in. Turn the official Android Auto off, or it competes for the same connection.
To connect wirelessly BetterAuto needs Bluetooth, nearby WiFi devices and the local network.
No paired Bluetooth devices: pair the dongle or the head unit in the phone\'s Bluetooth settings.
Not known yet if it offers wireless Android Auto
Connects by itself when you switch the car on, without opening the app. Each device you use keeps its own: with two (the car and another one) whichever is switched on connects.
While connected to the car, the phone also stays on your own WiFi instead of leaving it.
It didn\'t answer over Bluetooth. Check that it is on and near the phone.
It connected over Bluetooth but closed without sending its WiFi details: it may still be busy with the previous try. Try again in a few seconds.
Joined its WiFi, but Android Auto didn\'t start.
Shows when BetterAuto is connected to the car, with a button to send the audio there.
Shows what\'s playing on the car screen and on the dashboard, and lets you control it. Turn on BetterAuto in the list.
Allow audio access so the music plays in the car.
Works now, but Android asks for permission every time you connect. To skip it, run this once from a computer:
All set: the music goes to the car by itself when you connect.
All set, through Shizuku: the sound moves to the car with no prompt and no screen-sharing icon.
Android Auto is on and takes over the car connection. Open its page and tap Disable. If your phone doesn\'t allow it, run this from a computer:

With Shizuku, BetterAuto moves the phone\'s sound to the car like the official Android Auto: no permission prompt, no screen-sharing icon, the phone speaker is not muted, apps that block copying play too, and navigation prompts reach the car\'s speakers. With the USB cable it needs a rooted phone: without root, Shizuku stops as soon as the phone connects to the car, and BetterAuto goes back to copying the sound.
Without it the sound is copied, with those limits. Shizuku is free on the Play Store.
Installed but not running: open it and start it. Without root it stops after every restart of the phone and every time the phone connects to the car by cable.
Running: allow BetterAuto to use it.
Running, and BetterAuto is allowed to use it.

Direction of travel: the map turns with the car and looks ahead. North up: north always stays at the top.
How close the map is when it opens and when it comes back to the car. The knob still zooms in and out.
The map shows more road ahead as the car goes faster, and comes closer again in town. Turning the knob takes over until the map comes back to the car.
The limit of the road you are on, from OpenStreetMap: shown only where the map data states it, never guessed.
What the navigation says. Full: every instruction. Alerts only: just the arrivals at the stops and the destination. Mute: nothing. Also changed with the speaker button on the map.

Where the navigation\'s routes come from: a Valhalla server. Unless you set your own: Valhalla\'s public demo server, free but meant for trying, with no guarantee it is up. The places of your trip are sent to the server.
The address of a Valhalla server you run or trust. Port 8002 without http:// is taken as a server at home (http).
That is not a web address.
It answers (Valhalla %1$s): the next route comes from it.
No Valhalla server answers at this address. Check it, or that the phone can reach it.
Not on the home screen right now
Where I left off: the section you were in last time. Home: always the home screen.
How many widgets the home screen shows: one big one, two side by side, or one big and two small.
What each place of the home screen shows, and how big it is.
Tap a place to choose its widgets; drag the line between them to make them bigger or smaller.
The first one is shown; the others are a swipe away, or a press on the dots with the knob. Drag them to change the order. During a navigation the map comes forward by itself.
Which of the phone\'s calendars the calendar widget shows. New calendars show up by themselves.
Which weather app and which place: chosen in the BetterAuto app on the phone.
Day or night colors. Auto follows the car\'s headlights signal, or the phone when the car doesn\'t send it.
Where the bar with the sections goes. Auto: on the driver\'s side on wide screens, at the bottom on narrow ones.
Which side the driver sits: the bar and the big home widget go on that side. Auto: as the car says, left if it says nothing.
How big text, buttons and the map are drawn. Auto: as the car says for its screen. The screen is drawn again when it changes.
Order of the bar\'s buttons, which ones share a group and which are hidden. In the car you can also hold a button of the bar.
The time in the top bar. Like the phone: 24 or 12 hours as on the phone (or as the chosen date formats use).
The date next to the time in the top bar.
The bell in the top bar: how many notifications are waiting, and a tap opens them.
When the car connects, the music you were listening to carries on by itself.
Music apps with their own button in the app bar. In the car you can also hold an app\'s button to pin or unpin it.
Also sends the car the sound of apps that don\'t say what it is (a few players do). Off avoids stray sounds.
No notification pop-ups while driving; they still collect behind the bell.
Shows only who wrote and with which app. Auto: hidden while the car says someone else is aboard.

Notifications from group chats. Hide them to see only messages written to you.
Call and send messages by voice, with the steering wheel\'s voice button or the microphone button.

The answers are also spoken through the car\'s speakers, like \"Calling Mario Rossi\".

Kilometres and bar, or miles and psi, on the vehicle screens. Auto: as the phone\'s region uses.
°C or °F for temperatures. Auto: as the phone\'s region uses.
